title: Register of Infant Baptisms — Explanatory note on destruction of church records by 1880 cyclone
text:
REGISTER OF INFANT BAPTISMS.

No. | Name. | Parents. | By whom Baptized.

Savoy class was organized in 1873
by Rev. Graham and Milam.
It is supposed that a church register
was regularly kept until 1880.
On the night of 29th of May of that year,
occured the great cyclone in which the
church records were all destroyed.
Since that time there has been no regu-
lar secretary of Church Conference and no
effort made to keep a register. A list of the
names of the members was kept by H. W.
McQueen till 1890, when that was lost.
On 19th of Dec. 1891, the present secretary was
elected and instructed to make a compre-
register. To do this he had to depend upon
his own memory and such information as
could be gathered among the members.
Since the records are incomplete and
probably in some instances incorrect.
E. F. Grotts[?] Sec. C. C.
Third Quarterly Meeting Bills[?]ely 28, 1892
notes: This is a prefatory note at the beginning of the Register of Infant Baptisms explaining that the original church records were destroyed in the great cyclone of May 29, 1880. The class was organized in 1873 by Rev. Graham and Milam. H. W. McQueen kept a membership list until 1890 when it too was lost. The secretary (E. F. Grotts[?]) was elected Dec. 19, 1891 to reconstruct the register from memory and gathered information. Secretary's surname uncertain — could be Grotts, Grotto, or similar. 'Bills[?]ely' in the date line may be a place name or word — possibly 'Bilsley' or simply the word 'likely.'
